explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses the GROUP BY clause on the EMAIL column and the HAVING clause to filter out emails that appear more than once, while Q2 uses a subquery to achieve the same result. The difference lies in the way the GROUP BY and HAVING clauses are used in Q1, which can lead to different results if the EMAIL column contains NULL values.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should contain at least one NULL value in the EMAIL column to trigger the difference between Q1 and Q2. Q1 will not return any results because the GROUP BY clause will treat NULL values as distinct, and the HAVING clause will not filter out the NULL values. Q2, on the other hand, will return the NULL value because the subquery will treat it as a valid email address.
